:::{.callout-note .mb-4}
## Before you start
- [Prepare your data](prepare-your-data.qmd) for deposit
- Review Faculty Research Data Collection policies
- Have your CalNet ID ready
:::

## Request Upload Access

Submit a [deposit interest form](https://berkeley.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dhxkjrglLbPeVBI) with basic information about your dataset.

A member of Data + Digital Scholarship Services will review your request, grant you upload access, and follow up with next steps before you proceed.

## Log In and Create a Dataset

Log in to UC Berkeley Library Dataverse with your CalNet ID and navigate to the [Faculty Research Data Collection](https://datasets.lib.berkeley.edu/dataverse/oskidata).

Click "+ Add Data" → "New Dataset."

Select a dataset template that matches your subject area, or select "None." Templates pre-populate certain fields but don't limit what metadata you can enter.

:::{.callout-important}
If you don't see an **"+ Add Data"** button, your upload access may not yet be configured. Contact [librarydataservices@berkeley.edu](mailto:librarydataservices@berkeley.edu) to adjust your permissions.
:::

## Add Required Metadata

Fill out the following required fields:

- **Title** — main title of the dataset
- **Author** — people or organizations that created the dataset
- **Point of Contact** — entity users can contact; email required
- **Description** — summary of purpose, nature, and scope
- **Subject** — area of study

Hover over the <i class="bi bi-question-circle"></i> icon next to any field for its definition.

## Upload Files

Drag and drop files into the upload area, or click "Select Files to Add." To preserve folder structure, 
upload a `.zip` file. Maximum 1,000 files per batch — for larger deposits, see [API upload instructions on GitHub](https://github.com/librarydataservices/berkeley-dataverse-upload).

Dataverse automatically creates archival `.tab` versions of Stata, SPSS, R, Excel, CSV, and TSV files. Your originals are preserved.

Click "Save Dataset."

:::{.callout-tip}
A DOI is reserved as soon as you save. You can include it in manuscripts or grant applications now — it will resolve publicly once the dataset is published.
:::

## Add Supplementary Metadata

Return to the dataset page → Metadata tab → "Add + Edit Metadata"

Add all metadata relevant to your discipline. You don't need to complete every section, only those that apply to your dataset.

- Citation Metadata _(all deposits)_
- Geospatial Metadata
- Social Science and Humanities Metadata
- Astronomy and Astrophysics Metadata
- Life Sciences Metadata

## Set Terms and Access

Return to the dataset page → Terms tab → "Edit Terms Requirements" and select a license:

- [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) 
- [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- Or select "Custom Terms" to define your own terms of use

Optionally, you may enable a guestbook to collect user information before download. Select "Standard Guestbook — Faculty Research Data." Guestbooks are not generally recommended for open access datasets (e.g., CC0, CC BY 4.0).

For licensing guidance, contact Scholarly Communication and Information Policy: 
[schol-comm@berkeley.edu](mailto:schol-comm@berkeley.edu)

## Submit for Review

Click "Submit for Review" on the dataset page, confirm your license, and submit.

Your dataset will be reviewed following the [CURATE(D) model](https://conservancy.umn.edu/items/2449305b-4cdc-4fbc-9902-2795b020c939). A member of Data + Digital Scholarship services may suggest changes to improve reusability.

:::{.callout-warning}
Once published, a dataset cannot be deleted — only new 
versions can be created. See 
[Dataset Versions](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/user/dataset-management.html#dataset-versions) 
for details.
:::
